tips.comment: Mullins is back, and I prefer this over his other runner. Looks to have been carefully nursed back to form. Will hopefully take this before going on to bigger things next season.

This hurdle race should lie between the Willie Mullins pair, who both won last time to break their maiden tag over hurdles. If Toad Hall leads, he could be vulnerable to a late challenge from Dr Eggman.

Put up two mightily impressive novices-performances at Doncaster and Ascot and if getting an easy lead here is going to be hard to beat. Ran well in Listed company when just a length and a half behind a fair sort at Huntingdon and shouldn't be underestimated inbthus. Didn't stay in the Albert Bartlett and will appreciate this drop in trip and decent ground as long as they don't over water. Yard in good form and with four winners from last dozen sent out continue to go well. EW banker for me here.

Essentially 3 lbs lower than his last run. Running in a much weaker race this time. He was sent off 4/1 2nd favorite for the Martin Pipe at the festival last time out. He finished a well-beaten 7th. The fact he was backed in tells you the better was expected. He had won his previous 2 runs prior to that. Firstly, his win at Ascot was impressive enough, despite only beating the runner-up Double Powerful by a narrow margin. That form has worked out well enough with Double Powerful placing off 6 lbs and 10 lbs higher marks on his next 2 runs. His next win was impressive as well. He beat King Of The Road comfortably, pulling away at the line to win by over 2 lengths. Admittedly, the form of that win isn't anything to get excited about. If he can reproduce that Ascot form here, I'd say he's the one to beat this time.

Typhoon Flyer has only had five runs since his debut in September but has been placed three times and won two, with the latest run after a short break being a win by 15L in C4, which could be enough for this step up to C2.

Likely has more to offer for the Owen team after a break. Beat Star of Affinity on handicap debut at Ascot before Christmas, with that horse now 20 lbs higher in weights. Last time out was a decent 3rd behind Idem and I Am Max at Kelso, with I Am Max running well in stronger races since. Relishes decent ground, and this stiff track should be perfect.

Strong Foundations has got in this competitive handicap off a nice low weight and has the assistance of the excellent claimer Freddie Mitchell in the saddle to take off a further 3 lbs. He has got one or two really nice pieces of form and he ran very nicely last time out when stepped up to this sort of trip. He looks well over-priced at 25/1.

Open race here and a good chance for Spirits Bay. A couple of nice wins over hurdles so far and has been looking ready for this step up in trip. Finished 7th in the Imperial Cup LTO at Sandown, which wasn't a bad effort.
Had a good start to the season and comes here nice and fresh after a break. Likely more improvement to come and with no ground issues should be in the frame

Doyen Quest has got to be a good each-way shout back here in a repeat to win this race again. Obviously, something was amiss in all its runs since winning, but the Skelton team wouldn't put it back in unless they thought it must have a squeak.

ROYALE MARGAUX is a recent Listed-class winner beating some useful types and she could still be feasibly treated back in the handicap sphere if forgiven for her last start. She has course form and a sire who appears to produce racers who hold their form with age , so she could surprise.
Led for a long way in the Pertemps over 3 miles at the festival here last month before weakening and 12th of 24. He is twice a winner over further than today's trip and the drop in trip will suit.

Whatsupwithyou is eleven now, but he has a bit going for him here and may run well at big odds. He finished second in this to Doyen Quest, giving 6 lbs and now receives 7 lbs from that rival, so should be competitive. Add to that the fact that he is reunited with Ben Jones, from being amateur ridden on his last few starts, who has finished second three times in all his rides, and I believe he is a good each way bet at 28's with Bet365, four places. Never won in Class 2 but was only beaten half a length last year.

DISCO ANNIE looks an interesting outsider in what does seem on paper an open handicap. Notably unexposed over hurdles, Rebecca Menzies' mare has yet to be beaten in a handicap hurdle, and it would be a brave person to suggest the 7-y-o has yet reached her ceiling. Although switched to chasing in December, she held her form, and this return to hurdling, upped in distance, could see the selection improve the few pounds needed.

The handicapper has given him a chance here, leaving him on the same mark he ran off at the festival. He finished a decent 3rd in that festival handicap behind Caldwell Potter, beaten 8L by the winner. To be fair, he was sent off a 66/1 shot, so he certainly outran his odds behind arguably the most impressive winner of the whole festival. Obviously, the winner franked the form next time out, winning a Grade 1 novice at Aintree (Mildmay Novices), which makes this lad's run behind him at this course look sound enough. He's run in much stronger races than this in the past. Admittedly, he's still a maiden over obstacles, but as mentioned above, this race is weaker than the chase races he's been contesting. If he repeats that festival run here, I think he can go very close in this wide-open affair on these terms.

Cheltenham's April meeting takes on extra significance this year with the trainers' championship in the balance, but Irish trainer Willie Mullins holds a very strong hand. CLASSIC GETAWAY has been mixing with some good horses this season and has run consistently well, then won the Red Mills Chase at Gowran last time in good style. Solid chance here.

Won the Cheltenham trials over course and distance on penultimate start at the end of January but pulled up when sent off second favourite in the novice's chase at the Cheltenham Festival last month, also over course and distance. Made a bad mistake in that recent race which put paid to his chances but should go close if able to put that behind him and granted a clear round.
Won a grade 2 last year and lame when running badly at Aintree. Probably needed the run last time out and headgear back on today.

Lightly raced 7-year-old, 2 wins from 4 over fences. Had a bit in hand at the line when winning a useful contest four weeks ago. The better ground is a big plus. He can have another big run in him for this campaign.

Looks like a decent each way bet here with the Mullins pair taking up a good part of the market. The horse has good course form, is on a decent mark, and the claimer has a good record for this trainer.
Has won a couple of good races at this course, with the last one being the valuable Paddy Power Gold Cup in November. This drying ground will be a big advantage too.

Potentially overlooked in the market for this race. Hang In There came good last spring, came 2nd in this race last year, and then went on to win a Class 2 event at Uttoxeter. Subsequently, he had 2 more runner-up efforts and a 3rd place. Had 2 breaks through the winter which were disappointing, but this return to good ground and the handicapper dropping him to only 2lb higher than the last win gives him a chance.
The selection is bidding for a hat trick. It has been raised only 4 lb for its last month's victories at Hereford and Exeter. Ajp Kingdom looks the best of the rest.

Planned Paradise has been running consistently well over marathon distances and could reverse placings with Yes Day, who beat him into 2nd place at Exeter on four pounds better terms here. Sam Twiston-Davies, who rides well at Cheltenham, takes over on board.

Ask Brewster steps up in grade after trouncing the field at Chepstow on good ground. Impressive when attacking fences. Will enjoy running with 9lb less to carry due to stepping up in class. 2 wins from 6 chase efforts (both on good ground). Would be dangerous to write off if showing repeat performance.

Has been pulled up 2 runs ago, a placed run prior to that, then win at Kempton over 24f on good 4 runs back. Also, 28 days ago over 28.5f at Haydock again on good ground, graced the winner's enclosure again. Had a 2nd wind operation since last run and will appreciate the faster surface. May find 1 or 2 better today but fancy a placed run at decent odds.

Race 4 at Cheltenham today is the Brooklands Watches Golden Miller Racing Holman Handicap Chase (Class 3) for 5-year-olds and upwards over 5,652 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 9-year-old mare Jumping Jet from the Gordon Elliott yard, and will be ridden by D J Gilligan. This daughter of Getaway from the esteemed Gordon Elliott stable has some decent form to her name and should be a factor in this field. Rates a danger on best form.

Mahland makes chase debut in a competitive race but looked a stayer when blitzing the field on good ground at Uttoxeter. Looked stronger the longer the race progressed. Two point-to-point runs yielded a win and runner-up effort to Ask Brewster, who he re-opposes, who's a two-time winner over fences under rules. Only 8 starts so far, so totally unexposed. Hit form this time last year and will be a danger if taking hurdles form into chasing.

Fortescue is chanced in a tricky race to call but a long-distance chase. Henry Daly trained eleven-year-old has thrived over long distances in the past. Winner of six chase starts from 25 goes over fences and goes well fresh, so might be better for a recent break of 56 days. Former winner at Listed level who reached a peak career rating of 145 and ran second on first outing this season off OR135. May have a chance in this Class 3 grade off a mark of 122. Regular partner Hugh Nugent claims a 3lbs allowance.

Looks the one to beat here. A couple of nice wins last year and won over this trip in December. Won again just after that and despite losing a shoe last time out, was a good 2nd, staying on well over 2m 4f. Step back up to 3m looks likely to suit today.

This is a cracking 3 mile handicap hurdle and Long Draw was a strong fancy for the Pertemps at Cheltenham but didn't quite make the cut, so although he hasn't run since Boxing Day, he is bound to be fit for this, especially given his excellent trainer. Hope Street looks an obvious danger as he was being prepped to run a big race at Aintree but didn't turn up for some reason.

He's now 13 lbs higher than the mark he defied to win this race last term. If anything, I think he's improved since then. So, I suspect he can cope with the rise in weights. He finished 3rd in a much stronger race than this on seasonal reappearance, beaten 6L by the winner, The Wallpark. That horse has been contesting Grade 1 races since, finishing 4th in the Long Walk Hurdle, 3rd in the Stayers' Hurdle, then finished 4th in the Liverpool Hurdle last time out. That run mentioned above came off just a 2 lbs lower mark than this. He pulled up in the Pertemps on his penultimate run, admittedly finding the race far too hot to handle. He ran again just 8 days later with the first-time visor on. He absolutely bolted up, beating Welcome To The Cartries with plenty in hand. The visor is left on again this time. If he can repeat the last run, I think he could win this event for the 2nd year running.

This may require slightly different tactics from the jockey. Samuel Spade tends to be held up at the back in most races, and while he has often made late runs towards the finish, he sometimes doesn't get there. There's definitely a horse there, however, and he deserves support.

Beat a neck over course and distance off this mark of 119 in January 2024. Disappointed in both starts this year but will strip fitter for the two runs, and the recent wind surgery could help. Of interest back down to this mark of 119.
A return to hurdling and a drop in grade should spark some improvement for this 12-year-old, who has been a gallant servant to his connections.

The handicapper has left him on the same mark as last time out. Having run well again off his current mark. Admittedly, he's 10lbs above the mark he won off at this meeting last season. To be fair, the form of the win is fairly solid. He pulled a good 9L clear with the runner-up Midnight Our Fred. That rates decent form given the winner went on to run a cracker in an ultra-competitive renewal of the Paddy Power, finishing a clear 2nd behind Perceval Legallois. He's placed off his current mark on his last 3 runs. Firstly, in a competitive handicap at this track, he finished 3rd behind Abuffalosoldier, beaten 5L by the winner. On his penultimate run, he finished a clear 2nd behind Henry's Friend in the Mandarin. A decent performance given he jumped poorly. He finished a decent 3rd in the Grimthorpe last time out, beaten 5L by the winner Moroder. He gets a 6lbs weight swing with that horse this time. We know this lad likes this track, and Moroder is now 4lbs higher than his 2nd place finish in this event last year. I think Hymac can reverse the form.

Moroder could round off what could be a valuable day for the Mullins yard. Not getting any younger at 11, but the falling mark from high 130s to 125 last time brought an impressive win at Doncaster. The rating goes back up now, but the class of opposition doesn't, and it's a smaller field.

Java Point looks overpriced at 8/1 considering he's finished 2nd here at this course twice. Gavin Sheehan has won his last 2 rides and Henry Oliver won with his last entry at Warwick. Races off bottom weight with only 10st9lb to carry. Was 4th jumping last fence at Sandown over 3m on good ground and rallied to only be denied by a neck, should appreciate this step up to 3m2f based on that evidence.

Not been the greatest season for the Kim Bailey-trained 10-year-old. The handicap mark is dropping to a winnable mark, and good ground shouldn't be a problem. This race is wide open, with most rivals having plenty to prove.
Casa No Mento won last time out (as did others), but that win looks very good on paper. It is well treated here and can go in again for a trainer who knows how to get a Cheltenham winner.

Had run a number of excellent races before flopping badly last time. I am going to ignore that run and hope that the better ground will help the horse today. Has a good five-pound claimer aboard and after a decent break should be fresh.

Big Boy Bobby has returned from a long break with 2 eye catching runs - beaten 1 length by Ooh Betty (same jockey takes the ride) who was only beaten half a length in the Scottish Champion Hurdle and then seen off when runner up to a well backed and promising handicap debutant at Newcastle. Only win over obstacles was on good ground and a winner on good to firm on the flat - so the drier the ground the better for this selection. Alan King horses are in good nick (won the Champion Chase at Ayr) and a further 3 runner up efforts from last 8 runs. NAP

He has to put behind him a poor run last time out when he tried chasing, which he didn't seem to enjoy. He's run a couple of decent races here at Cheltenham. Still lightly raced, I'll take a chance he can make the frame at least here.

LUNAR SOVEREIGN is an attractive price for a runner who is well treated on his best efforts and who could step forward considerably on the back of his return from a huge absence. He ran with credit last month and still not highly-tried for a nine year old having familiarised himself with his new yard he could surprise.

I'm going to take a chance on Ashington, who I believe is overpriced at 22/1. He put in a solid performance last time out, finishing 5th of 16 at Kelso, and had previously scored a win off a mark of 115. With Tom Midgley taking 3lb off, Ashington effectively returns to that same winning mark for this upcoming race at Cheltenham. While his form has been a bit inconsistent, I think the good ground will play to his strengths. Given his previous performances and current mark, he looks capable of outrunning his odds. At this price, I'm happy to have an each-way bet, as the value is certainly there.

This 10 year old, a 2 time winner of handicap hurdles during the 2020/21 season, has achieved 4 victories since then, including a recent win over fences at Ayr in January. He has delivered commendable performances in his recent outings, and with an experienced jockey holding a 7lb claim, he stands a good chance of surpassing his 4th place result in the 2023 race. Betting each-way at 25/1 offers excellent value.

Ali Shuffle got the job done on her debut at Redcar. Travelled well that day and round here this will help against a big field of mainly newcomers. Turned out quickly which makes me a bit more confident this will go in again.

Well-bred newcomer from a yard that can have them ready for debut. The stable already had a two-year-old winner, and this one is bred to be fast. The pedigree suggests this one might take some beating.

This Mattmu filly comes from a lightly-raced dam who is half-sister to the impressive 2-year-old winner, Hears of Fire, who has triumphed at distances ranging from 5f to 1m. David Allan will be her jockey, and she looks to be the first choice among the 3 runners from the Easterby team. While her winning prospects are debatable, she has a strong chance of finishing in the top positions, making her a promising each-way bet at 28/1.

Azure Angel found the Listed company a bit much last time but had been in good form on the AW before that. She’s back below her last winning mark and should be more competitive here, though she’s unproven over 5f and will need a strong pace to bring out her best late run.

Trilby has been improving with four sprint wins last year but had a bit of trouble on the return from a break last month when 12th after getting held up in C3 at 6f. I think the combination of getting back to 5f and being second up could see him bounce back.

Being drawn in stall 1 over 5f at Beverley has a huge advantage. Factor in Elegant Erin's course record of 3 C&D wins from 5 runs (one of those defeats was in a class 1 listed event) and her top speed rating of the field - 7/1 looks way too big a price. Won off a rating 1lb lower than today's at this C&D in 2022 before the mark started to slide. Has bounced back with 3 wins in the last 9 runs.

The weather still looks a little unpredictable, but based on the recent forecast, I suspect Grace Angel will run a big race at decent odds here. Has some decent stats coming into this, and the jockey booking is a positive.

Equity Law hasn’t been firing lately and was well held at Lingfield last time, but he’s back on turf now which should suit better. He’s sliding down the weights and the trainer does really well at Beverley, so while there’s a bit to prove off a break, he’s not one to completely rule out.

GOOD EARTH could strip fitter for the run last time out at Southwell (first in 146 days). Ended last season a bit off-color, but the runs at York and Doncaster were on soft ground and tasty-looking lucrative races for the grade. Now comes to firmer ground, with fewer competitors to worry about and has avoided a really high draw. Each-way claims for sure.

Hiya Maite came close at Southwell last time and although he’s on a long losing run, he’s clearly in good nick and this sharp track should play to his strengths. He’s 5lb lower on turf than AW, which gives him a real chance of snapping that drought here.
Won first time up last season and reappears today off the same mark as she finished her season in October, finishing a decent 2nd. Should go close in this.

Previous course and distance winner. Needs a career best to win this but ran 2 decent races at the end of last season. Unlucky not to win from a 4lb lower mark and then running 3rd off today's mark, so has an each-way chance.

Adoon Valley did too much too soon at Newmarket on her second start, but that run came quickly after a promising debut, and the form from that first outing has been strongly franked. She’s back from a break now, up in trip, and looks a major player if she’s trained on as expected.
The type that should improve for the trip and is the value bet against the favorite who has achieved nothing as yet.
Finished 10 of 12 in U.K. flat debut at Lingfield last November. Although she did not show much ability in that outing, she is from a top yard, so I think good things are to come from her.

Sir Peter Fossick ran a decent race at Chester when third and shaped like the extra distance here could be a plus. The handicap mark looks a touch high for now, but with a good jockey booked and improvement likely, he’s not without a chance.
I like the look of the horse running at today's trip. I also like the jockey/trainer combo and think they could have a very good day today.

Nibras Gold hasn’t been seen on the Flat in a while and was below par over fences last time, but he’s got some solid old form and could be dangerous if fully tuned up. Probably wants further ideally, but if there’s support and he’s sharp enough, he’s not out of it.
Ran well last at Doncaster and is on a winnable mark. Will appreciate the stiff 1m4 and is overpriced in my opinion.
Has an excellent course record of runs 1m2f and beyond. Form of 1-2-1-3, including one win at C&D. Only 1lb higher than the last win. Record fresh is a concern.

Sisterandbrother was way out of his depth last time but drops back into calmer waters here and returns to 12f, which suits much better. He’s hit and miss but capable on his day so he could run better than his price suggests.

Law Degree has been knocking on the door since entering handicaps and went down by just a neck at Redcar last time. He’s consistent, the drop to 7f should be fine, and with a top trainer at Beverley, he looks ready to get his head in front.

Seed Investor didn’t get the clearest run at Southwell last time but still ran with credit, and his overall profile is solid. Cheekpieces go on for the first time, conditions look spot on, and while he may just need this after the break, he’s got a definite chance if tuned up.

Berkshire Smudge is still without a win but has a chance to shed that maiden tag in a race that lacks any real quality. He takes a drop in class, and the return to turf might suit as his last two runs were on the AW.
Sovereign Class looked class when finishing 2nd last time out. Although this looks a tough affair, it has a weight advantage and shouldn't worry too much about the draw. 4 places at 10s looks value.
Just a lightly raced maiden who has performed well on turf, so should welcome a return back to turf tomorrow. He has a chance if he can take advantage of the dropped mark.

SUZETTE won a nursery handicap from this mark at Carlisle in August, before being unsuccessfully tried at a higher grade at Ayr and York. First run as a 3yo was after a lengthy break so is forgiven and she could fare better now back to this grade and weight. Stable not in bad form and tend to do better with the sprinters.

Crowns Lady went forward too hard at Newcastle last time but wasn’t beaten far and 7f looks like her sweet spot. She stays a mile, has some decent form in the book, and should run her race if ready to go.

Mick Easterby has a decent hand here and this one especially could start off well this season off her lowest mark. She has form at 1m in a class 2 and back in calmer waters could be ready to fire from 9 months off. Not sure where Jo Mason is but Tom Eaves might get a better tune, you never know.
Has won in the past over CD after a similar break. Was running fairly well last year so hopefully she has retained some of that talent now at eight years old.

Coming bang into form with a couple of recent fourths, and the stiff uphill finish at Beverley will definitely help as the horse keeps staying on in its races on flatter tracks. Still just three pounds above its last winning mark, this represents a really good chance for another victory.

Mystical Maria didn’t quite see it out over 11f last time, so the drop back in trip should suit much better. She’s shown ability in shorter races and if settling into a good rhythm, she’s got a fair chance of getting involved here.
Achieved 3 wins from 18 runs last year but is also a 5-time course winner. This outing will be a bit tricky going up in class, but has won 3 of her last 4 runs, so has bags of ability.

Since her last win in 2024, she has participated in 14 races. 8 days ago, she secured a respectable 8th place out of 13 in a handicap at Southwell, demonstrating a solid performance in the final stretch. As she steps onto turf for the first time, she may not have the accolades of others, but there's a strong chance for her to make considerable progress. At odds of 25/1, she offers great value for an each-way bet.

History suggests that those rated in the 90s (nearly half the field) will struggle to give weight to one rated in the 80s, and this Charlie Appleby one could well be the answer with William Buick booked. The pair had a good day one at the meeting, and this horse has some very good collateral form to delve into, which strongly suggests that he looks on a good mark here judging by the quality of the horses he's been beating or finishing close to. Cheekpieces go on now too to squeeze out further improvement, and he looks great value to me at 9/2.

Scored first time up last year, finishing off his first season of racing when sent off at just 7/1 in the Group 1 Middle Park. Soft ground that day did not look to suit him so the rain on Tuesday is not ideal but the conditions are not anything like as bad. Starts off from 94 in a handicap which could be a tempting opening mark if connections think that he is a genuine Group 1 type.
He will be high up in the market and has the big edge potentially of having had a prep race for this. So fitness should be on his side today.
Double Rush showed significant improvement to win last time at Wolverhampton and could be attractively weighted for his first start in a handicap this afternoon.

The 3yo has 2 wins from 4 and plenty of room for improvement on his return from a 6 month break. Beaten 2L on his last start, a decent looking Listed contest - didn’t have a smooth passage that day. His opening handicap mark of 93 could prove to be lenient.
Cayman Tai could get at least a place here off bottom weight in this handicap. He finished 2nd at Pontefract last week and is due to go up a pound for that run shortly.

3-year-old Havana Gold colt. Won last time out over 6 furlongs on heavy ground, but perhaps the better form was the two 2nd places at Newbury and York, both also over 6 furlongs. Well drawn, yard in decent form, and do well with their runners at Newmarket.

MAJESTIC WAVE ran with credit on his seasonal reappearance when all-weather racing. He is a former Irish trained three year old colt who showed some decent form through qualifying and assuming he builds on his comeback run now switched to turf he could get competitive.

King Of Bears wasn’t disgraced in the Richmond and has had excuses since, including just the one run after and a subsequent wind op. He returns from a break with a hood fitted and definite ability in the book so worth keeping an eye on.

Altareq is bred in the purple as a full-brother to the classy Al Asifah and by Frankel out of a high-quality mare, so stamina and talent are likely there. The yard runs two and both look strong on paper, making it tough to split them, but he’s clearly got a big reputation and should go well first time out.

With J&T Gosden among winners' enclosures yesterday, and winners of this race two out of the last five, the Cracksman colt won't be outdone come final furlong. Likely to do well further than a mile, as per the very smart dam, a start from a high draw in 10th gate is a plus.
One of many newcomers in the race, but the fact he has already been gelded suggests they want him to be forward early on.
His dam's side was very strong in France, and that is often the more instructive side. Wasn't cheap either and should be forward.

A Saxon Warrior colt, whose dam is a Swedish winner at 1 and half miles and a half-sister to the accomplished Inaya, a winner up to 1 and three quarter miles. With the talented Joe Leavy set to ride this promising 3 year old from the successful Hannon stable, the 50/1 odds for an each-way bet present an irresistible opportunity.

Only 2/11 winning favorites, however, 8/12 top 3 in the betting. Decent form over 6f and 7f last season, including a comeback G3 win to beat Ramatuelle. Then 0.5L 4th in the French Guineas before Jean Prat flop. Back in business this season with G2 2nd in Meydan over a mile and a listed win back at 6f. Looks now as if she'll be campaigned as a sprinter and being in receipt of weight all around her has the perfect opportunity to make a winning return to home soils.

Might have the fitness edge on the rest, having won nicely at Chantilly a month ago. The ease in the ground may suit him better than Romantic Style, who has wintered in Dubai and should also be fit after two runs in January in Meydan, but may find this 6f a bit short now.
The form of his recent win has worked out well. The race before that was a good second at Doncaster, where the winner has since won.

Hopefully, it would have shaken off some rust from the LTO effort when only 11 of 14 here over C&D last April. To be fair, it was the first run since 2023, so hoping for improvements that will finally end the long losing run as it's now been 690 days since the last win.

Grand Grey held his own in good company last season and wasn’t disgraced in the Prix de l’Abbaye, finishing midfield in a strong Group 1. He’s tough and consistent, the yard took this race last year, and he looks set to go well again.
Had some good form as a 2 year old and was bogged down at Doncaster on the soft going. The going should dry up and good going will be fine. The one to beat.

Opera Ballo looks worth a play in the Craven Stakes. One of two Charlie Appleby (SR 31%) runners and the choice of James Doyle (SR 28%). Brings an unusual route here. Two 'impressive' wins over 1 mile at Kempton where he travelled strongly latterly and ran prominently each time. Coming in for market support here and taken to beat the more experienced rivals in a smart looking Craven Stakes.
The 4th at Longchamp was on heavy ground, where all of his best form comes on a sound surface like he will get today at Newmarket.
Aomori City is proven at this level and is also the mount of William Buick here. At the odds, I don't think you can pass up this horse.

New Century looked a real prospect at two, progressing nicely and landing the Stonehenge Stakes in good style. He shaped like a mile suits him well and with more improvement likely this season, he’s definitely in the mix on return.

A bit of a flier, but we've seen shocks in this in the past. With the rain falling, I wouldn't be surprised to see the ground riding on the softer side. The Waco Kid won the Group 3 Tattersalls Stakes here in September, making all on soft ground to win by 2.75L over 7f. The 2nd almost won a Listed contest next time (neck 2nd), and the 5th has won twice as a 3yo, so there's some substance there (rest unraced since). I can forgive him being run off his feet on rattling quick ground at Del Mar next time. This looks a pretty strong contest on paper, but with conditions potentially to suit and with plenty of experience under his belt, I can see a shock on the cards, with others maybe having bigger targets later in the season.
Hadn't finished outside of the top two prior to a heavy ground 4th to finish last term. Back on good ground today and being overlooked at a massive price here.
Stellenbosch should be much shorter here, and I think that Ryan Moore taking the ride for Coolmore connections is another positive here too.

Swiss Lightning showed little on debut but comes from a top yard in form and is bred to do better with time. He’s got plenty to find on paper but looks the type to take a big step forward second time out.

Showed promise in a couple of juvenile events and returned after an 8 month absence in a mile race at Kempton but was on her toes in the preliminaries and didn’t show her form. Should be more at home over this trip and worth a second look.

Lady Of The Isles failed in its debut this December in a mile at Kempton. But connections make us think that it would be much better today. The shorter distance, with Rossa Ryan on the saddle this time, will help its cause.

Valedictory showed loads of promise on debut when a close third at Doncaster and looked to have plenty left in the tank. Steps up in trip which should suit, and with a top jockey and leading yard behind him, he’s the one they all have to beat.

Stardrop was not bad after a duff start on debut last month when fourth of nine and seemed to be getting the hang of things on the run-in. So, worth another shot now second up, but with Harry Davies this time EW.

Fifty Nifty looked a smart prospect last year, winning both starts including a smooth handicap success off 87 on the July Course. He’s up 6lb and returns from a break, but remains unexposed and likely has more to come.

Ran a very good race first time up last year when running on strongly at the finish to finish a close-up third. Started last year on a mark of 78 and was progressive, finishing on a mark of 91 (today's mark). Trainer has horses running above expectations at present.

The model I run suggests Buckna for this race tomorrow. Highest RPR of the field, with equal weight being carried across the horses. Buckna comes here with good form and should be able to get over the line.

I'm going to take on the favourite, Buckna, and second favourite, Devon Dude, at the moment with Guchen. He's had some pretty good results at Hereford and Huntington last time out with a 2nd and 3rd. He now comes to Ffos Las with 11st 5lbs on his back but with 10lb claimer Nathan Andrews. So this puts him well in with a chance to strike. Hopefully, this grey gelding goes well and likes it at Ffos Las.

The model I run suggests Kap Boy to come in first ahead of Golan Loop in second and Pyleigh Master in third. This horse has the highest RPR, highest OR, and no penalty in weights. Harry Cobden on board is in great form and should be able to lead the horse over the line first.

Ran his best race yet at Exeter last time when back down at 17f having made his hurdles debut over 26f. That last run saw him taking 4th spot late on and given his likely SP looks a fair each way prospect.

Star Walking looked to appreciate three miles last time when held up at Doncaster but did not get a clear run through when only 4th in a Listed novice hurdle. Back to a handicap she should do much better than her only previous handicap at Fakenham when an underperforming well beaten favourite and Harry Cobden is booked to ride.

Ran right up to form, only beaten 6L when fourth in a mares' novice hurdle Grade 2 over 2m 5f at Newbury. Now down in grade but up in trip. If stamina holds out, the trainer is confident it will, then solid each way NAP for me today.
8-year-old mare has been running well in chases and finished second in her last two chase races. Handicapped fairly, she has serious claims in this now reverting back to hurdles.

Is coming here after a small break, and past runs prove this is a positive. CD winner as well. Looks to be on a lenient mark.

The model I run has simulated this race and has El Granjero coming in first ahead of Kado De Joie in second and West to the Bridge in third. El Granjero has the joint second highest RPr of the field and steps out with a reasonable weight to carry for the 2m 4f trip. Ned Fox on board has 3 lbs claiming, which helps lower the ask and just tilts the race to favor.
Eaton Anne won a couple of handicaps during the winter, disappointing last time out but worth another chance at these big odds.
First run since May 2023, so could understandably be rusty. But has won here before, the last run out, and four wins in a short career so far across hurdles and flat.

The model I run suggests Airtothethrone can win this one. The horse has the highest RPR and OR of the field but has the highest weight to carry to offset that. This horse is a course and distance winner only 2 weeks ago and looks set to add here. Lewis Saunders is on board and has 7 lbs claiming, meaning that when you net out the weights, Airtothethrone is only carrying a 'middle of the pack' weight.

Another Lord was run out of it over course and distance ten days ago by Airtothethrone but could get his revenge on seven pounds better terms, not including seven-pound claimer Lewis Saunders taking over on Airtothethrone. Yet to win this season, he has been 2nd three times.
Although his last run wasn't great, he should still have plenty of potential. He wasn't that far behind Final Demand over this trip in a PTP.

Try The Money has run well at this track a few times without winning and was closest to doing so when staying on 3rd over hurdles here - 2m4f good to soft last April. Has been chasing since and learning this game, proving he has the stamina for 3m in the process. On a low mark and looks like he still has more to offer. Big chance if putting it all in today.

The model I run has Just Aidan to win this one, coming in ahead of Highbury Hill in second and Rodney in third. This result has been driven by Just Aidan having the second highest RPR of the 12 runners, but a kind OR meaning slightly less weight to carry than the rest of the market leaders.

Good Impression was only just over 3l behind L'Empire Burt last time. That was the 10-year-old's first run for 153 days, and he looked very much like he would benefit from it. The CD winner will act even if there is some rain and looks to have solid claims of a place at the very least.

KYLENOE DANCER is interesting making her debut at the foot of the weights for a high-profile trainer combination. It also catches the eye that ace jockey Harry Cobden comes to Ffos Las for a late ride on a Wednesday evening. Maybe in her time spent absent this mature mare has improved considerably and this is a weak handicap hurdle which will not take much winning.
